papers.title: Multi-omics profiling of oral microbial functional signatures and systemic immune-metabolic features in perinatal depression.
papers.abstract: Perinatal depression (PND) occurs during a period marked by profound endocrine, metabolic, and immune adaptation. Although alterations in immune-metabolic regulation have been reported in PND, how such changes manifest across distinct biological compartments remains unclear. The oral mucosal ecosystem represents an immunologically active interface with direct connections to systemic circulation, yet its functional characteristics in PND have been insufficiently explored. In this study, we examined whether PND is characterized by differences in oral microbial functional profiles alongside syste
papers.summary: This study profiles oral microbial functional signatures and systemic immune-metabolic features in perinatal depression (PND), finding that PND is associated with distinct oral microbial functional profiles and coordinated systemic immune-metabolic alterations. The work highlights the oral mucosal ecosystem as a relevant interface for understanding PND pathophysiology.

papers.title: Macrogenomic analysis showcases the diversity of tick RNA viruses in Mentougou, Beijing, China.
papers.abstract: Ticks are the second most significant vector of human pathogens worldwide, with 911 documented species globally and a broad distributed across China. Currently, over 160 tick-borne viruses (TBVs) have been identified, several of which pose substantial threats to human health, such as Dabie bandavirus, Jingmen tick virus, Alongshan virus, Songling virus, Beiji nairovirus, and Langya henipavirus, raising increasing global attention. Despite their significance, the diversity of TBVs in Beijing remains poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the diversity of RNA viruses in ticks collected from Mentougou, Beijing, revealing a wide range of tick-borne viruses and highlighting the region's under-explored viral diversity. The findings underscore the need for enhanced surveillance of tick-borne pathogens in urban-adjacent areas of China.

papers.title: PIMENTO: A primer inference toolkit to facilitate large-scale calling of amplicon sequence variants.
papers.abstract: The identification of amplicon sequence variants from DNA metabarcoding data is a common method for revealing the taxonomic makeup of environmental samples, and for allowing comparative studies between similar datasets. A significant hurdle to the large-scale calling of amplicon sequence variants from publicly available nucleotide datasets is the heterogeneous presence of primer sequences in reads, the removal of which is a necessary pre-processing step for this form of analysis. Furthermore, as the details of the experimental primers are rarely captured in the metadata associated with the seq
papers.summary: PIMENTO is a new toolkit that automates the detection and removal of primer sequences from DNA metabarcoding data, addressing a major bottleneck in large-scale amplicon sequence variant (ASV) calling. By inferring primers directly from reads, it enables more efficient and accurate processing of publicly available datasets without relying on incomplete metadata.

papers.title: Non-pharmacological interventions for lactational mastitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
papers.abstract: Lactational mastitis is a common inflammatory condition that can adversely affect maternal well-being and is associated with early cessation of breastfeeding. Although antibiotics and analgesics are widely used in clinical practice, concerns regarding antimicrobial resistance and potential effects on the infant microbiome have prompted increasing interest in non-pharmacological approaches. A range of physical and biological interventions, including probiotics, therapeutic ultrasound, acupuncture and manual therapies, have been investigated; however, the comparative effectiveness and safety of
papers.summary: This protocol outlines a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate non-pharmacological interventions for lactational mastitis, such as probiotics, ultrasound, and acupuncture. The study aims to compare their effectiveness and safety, addressing growing concerns about antibiotic use and its impact on the infant microbiome.

papers.title: CAMEO: a CAZyme mapping engine optimized for HUMAnN.
papers.abstract: There are technical barriers to creating functional mapping databases and a dearth of validated databases that can be easily implemented by users. We present CAMEO, a precomputed and validated mapping file for carbohydrate-active enzymes, as well as an approach to building new CAZyme mapping files, for use with HUMAnN.
papers.summary: CAMEO provides a precomputed, validated mapping file for carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) that can be used directly with the HUMAnN functional profiling tool, overcoming technical barriers to creating such databases. It also offers a method for users to build their own CAZyme mapping files, making CAZyme analysis more accessible.

papers.title: Viruses help shape microbiome response to polyphenol rewiring of methane-suppressed peat microcosms.
papers.abstract: Human activities are accelerating permafrost thaw and subsequent methane emissions from increased microbial activity, prompting microbiome engineering efforts as an emissions mitigation strategy. We recently demonstrated that catechin amendment could drastically reduce methane emissions (>80%) in peat microcosms by enriching catechin-degrading prokaryotes that outcompeted methanogens for hydrogen. However, viral contributions to such microbiome-level responses remain unexplored and we hypothesized that viral dynamics could help shape the microbiome response as nutrient amendments may alter cel
papers.summary: This study investigates how viruses influence the microbiome response to polyphenol (catechin) amendment in peat microcosms, a strategy previously shown to reduce methane emissions. The authors find that viral dynamics, likely through infection of key prokaryotes, help shape the microbial community restructuring that underlies methane suppression, highlighting a previously overlooked role for viruses in microbiome engineering outcomes.

papers.title: Bacterial-based cancer therapy: mechanisms and therapeutic advances.
papers.abstract: Targeted cancer therapies increasingly require platforms that can penetrate poorly perfused tumor regions while minimizing systemic toxicity. Bacteria, owing to their intrinsic tumor tropism, genetic programmability, and immunostimulatory properties, have re-emerged as versatile anticancer agents, ranging from attenuated tumor-colonizing strains to highly engineered "living therapeutics." In this review, we synthesize the mechanistic foundations and therapeutic advances of bacterial-based cancer therapy through four major themes. First, we examine foundational mechanisms, including tumor-selec
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the mechanistic foundations and therapeutic advances of bacterial-based cancer therapy, highlighting how bacteria's intrinsic tumor tropism, genetic programmability, and immunostimulatory properties make them versatile anticancer agents. It covers foundational mechanisms and the development of engineered 'living therapeutics' for treating poorly perfused tumors with reduced systemic toxicity.

papers.title: Nanopore sequencing reveals coordinated host and microbiome responses across barley genotypes.
papers.abstract: Barley (Hordeum vulgare L.) provides a suitable model for studying domestication-driven plant-microbiome interactions. Although wild, landrace, and modern genotypes host distinct rhizosphere communities, the extent to which roots and microbes reciprocally influence each other remains unclear. Here, we applied an integrated multi-omics approach combining long-read metagenomics, root transcriptomics, and plant genomics to understand genotype-specific host-microbiome coordination.
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated multi-omics approach combining long-read metagenomics, root transcriptomics, and plant genomics to investigate how different barley genotypes (wild, landrace, and modern) coordinate with their rhizosphere microbiomes. The findings reveal genotype-specific host-microbiome interactions, providing insights into domestication-driven changes in plant-microbe relationships.

papers.title: Evolution of the fecal and oral microbiota after prophylactic antibiotics administered for dental surgeries.
papers.abstract: The human oral and gut microbiomes play critical roles in maintaining overall health. Although systemic antibiotics are frequently prescribed perioperatively in dental procedures, their impact on microbiota composition and diversity remains inadequately understood. The authors' objective was to characterize the evolution of the gut and oral microbiomes after a course of antibiotics administered for dental surgeries. The authors hypothesized that the microbiome would experience disruption but eventually recover to baseline levels and that patient-related factors would influence the extent of di
papers.journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
papers.summary: This study characterizes how a course of prophylactic antibiotics for dental surgeries affects the gut and oral microbiomes, finding that while the microbiota experiences disruption, it eventually recovers to baseline levels, with patient-related factors influencing the extent of disturbance. The findings highlight the need to consider microbiome impacts when prescribing antibiotics perioperatively.

papers.title: The Gut-brain-adipose Axis in Ultra-processed Food and Obesity: A Mechanistic Synthesis and Its Implications for Food Classification.
papers.abstract: Consumption of ultra-processed food (UPF) tracks closely with obesity across populations, and the Nova classification has become the dominant tool for capturing that exposure. Why UPF promotes weight gain is a separate question, and the biological answer has accumulated in fragments. I draw those strands together and ask whether three mechanisms usually studied in isolation: gut microbial disruption, hypothalamic inflammation, and adipose tissue dysfunction, are better understood as one connected system, and what that would mean for how UPF is classified.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence linking ultra-processed food consumption to obesity through three interconnected mechanisms—gut microbial disruption, hypothalamic inflammation, and adipose tissue dysfunction—proposing they operate as a unified gut-brain-adipose axis. The author argues that recognizing this systemic connection could inform more biologically meaningful food classification systems beyond the current Nova framework.

papers.title: Innovative Test Strip-Based Colorimetric Sensors Integrated With Affinity Chromatography: Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitor Screening Breakthrough in Lycium Barbarum Leaves.
papers.abstract: Current Alzheimer's drugs exhibit limited effectiveness, highlighting the necessity for multi-target treatments. This study developed an innovative and efficient screening platform combining hydrogen peroxide test strip-based colorimetric sensing with affinity chromatography for rapid identification of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors from complex herbal medicines. Applying this strategy, from Lycium barbarum leaves, we identified three potent inhibitors: chlorogenic acid, N-acetyl-N'-caffeoylputrescine (NANCP), and N-caffeoylputrescine (NCP), with IC50 ranging from 55.7 to 143.2 µm. Mol
papers.summary: This study presents a new screening platform that combines hydrogen peroxide test strip-based colorimetric sensing with affinity chromatography to rapidly identify acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors from complex herbal mixtures. Using this approach, the authors discovered three potent AChE inhibitors from Lycium barbarum leaves, with IC50 values in the micromolar range, offering a potential multi-target strategy for Alzheimer's disease treatment.

papers.title: Strain-level ecological filtering governs microbial colonization of the human gut.
papers.abstract: Microbial colonization of the human gut is typically inferred from species-level profiling, yet durable establishment operates at the strain level. Here, using longitudinal shotgun metagenomics across multiple donor-recipient pairs undergoing fecal microbiota transplantation, we show that colonization is governed by lineage-dependent strain-level ecological filtering. Strain-resolved analyses reveal that gut colonization imposes reproducible population-genetic bottlenecks, characterized by reduced nucleotide diversity and selective strain capture. Lineage identity is the primary determinant of
papers.summary: This study uses longitudinal shotgun metagenomics from fecal microbiota transplant recipients to show that gut colonization is governed by strain-level ecological filtering, not just species-level dynamics. The authors find reproducible population-genetic bottlenecks with reduced nucleotide diversity and selective strain capture, where lineage identity is the primary determinant of successful colonization.

papers.title: Assessing the Relationship between Gut Microbiota and Kidney Stones: A Two-Sample Mendelian Randomization Analysis.
papers.abstract: There is increasing evidence that gut microbiota is associated with the risk of kidney stones diseases (KSD), but whether a causal relationship exists remains unclear. We used the Mendelian randomization (MR) method to assess the potential causal relationship between gut microbiota and KSD risk.
papers.summary: This study used Mendelian randomization to investigate whether gut microbiota composition causally influences the risk of kidney stone disease. The findings suggest a potential causal relationship for certain microbial taxa, providing evidence that gut microbiota may play a role in kidney stone formation.

papers.title: Lachnospiraceae and Its Metabolite Malate Act in Concert to Repair Gut Microbiota Imbalance and Block Colorectal Cancer Progression.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis is a crucial driver of the initiation and progression of colorectal cancer (CRC), where functional gut microbes and their metabolites play key roles in the microecological regulation of CRC. Currently, the association between Lachnospiraceae and CRC progression, as well as the underlying mechanisms, remains incompletely understood and warrants further investigation.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of Lachnospiraceae and its metabolite malate in colorectal cancer (CRC), finding that they work together to repair gut microbiota imbalance and block CRC progression. The findings suggest a potential therapeutic avenue targeting this microbial-metabolite axis for CRC management.

papers.title: MeioBIOME: A snakemake workflow for the parallel analysis of meiofaunal genomes and host-associated bacteria/archaea.
papers.abstract: Microbes closely interact with every living organism, including meiofauna (i.e., microbial eukaryotes 38 μm - 1 mm in length), and influence the development, life cycle, and evolution of diverse metazoans. Together, meiofauna and their microbiomes, collectively referred to as the holobiont, underpin biogeochemical cycles and drive decomposition of organic matter. However, our understanding of the ecological and evolutionary dynamics of meiofauna microbiomes are limited, typically owed to low-resolution 16S rRNA surveys, which cannot accurately delineate bacterial taxa. Single-specimen holobion
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MeioBIOME is a new Snakemake workflow that enables parallel analysis of meiofaunal genomes and their associated host bacteria/archaea from single-specimen samples. It addresses the limitations of low-resolution 16S rRNA surveys by providing a scalable, reproducible pipeline for high-resolution genomic and metagenomic analysis of holobionts.

papers.title: Host phylogeny and diet shape gut microbiome and virome in wild small mammals of Gongga Mountain, China.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiotas play pivotal roles in host adaptation, yet their composition and function in high-altitude small mammals remain poorly characterized. This study investigated how host phylogeny (order-level) and dietary habits shape the gut microbiome and virome of three mammalian orders (Eulipotyphla, Rodentia, Lagomorpha) in Gongga Mountain, a biodiversity hotspot on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau. Metagenomic sequencing of 219 samples from 22 species revealed order-specific microbial signatures: Eulipotyphla (carnivorous) harbored higher abundances of potential pathogens (e.g., Helicobacter, Haf
papers.summary: This study characterizes the gut microbiome and virome of 22 wild small mammal species across three orders in Gongga Mountain, China, using metagenomic sequencing. It finds that host phylogeny and diet shape microbial community composition, with carnivorous Eulipotyphla harboring more potential pathogens, providing new insights into high-altitude host-microbe interactions.

papers.title: Antimicrobial peptides in anti-infective and immunomodulatory applications: Mechanisms, challenges, and emerging computational design.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial Peptides (AMPs) evolutionarily conserved effectors of innate immunity, have emerged as multifunctional agents with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, immunomodulatory capabilities, and potential applicability in cancer therapy. Despite their functional diversity and biological potency, the clinical translation of AMPs remains constrained by significant challenges, including proteolytic instability, hemolytic toxicity, high production costs, and protracted development pipelines. This review examines how the diverse molecular mechanisms through which AMPs exert antimicrobial ef
papers.summary: This review summarizes the mechanisms, challenges, and emerging computational design strategies for antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) in anti-infective and immunomodulatory applications. It highlights the multifunctional roles of AMPs, including broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity and potential in cancer therapy, while addressing key barriers to clinical translation such as proteolytic instability, hemolytic toxicity, and high production costs. The paper emphasizes the growing role of computational approaches in overcoming these challenges.

papers.title: A robust, sensitive phylogenetic method enables gene-level metagenomic analyses.
papers.abstract: A key goal in the microbiome field is to move from taxonomic associations towards mechanistic hypotheses about microbial gene function. However, most methods for linking microbiome changes to specific genes are biased towards finding marker genes, with weak evidence for functional relevance. Phylogenetic regression can address this issue and has been previously applied to changes in microbial prevalence, but many environments (such as the gut in health vs. disease) are characterized more by changes in abundance, which presents unique statistical challenges. We show that when applied to real di
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a new phylogenetic regression method designed to link microbiome abundance changes to specific microbial genes, addressing statistical challenges that arise with abundance data. The method is shown to be robust and sensitive in real datasets, enabling more reliable gene-level metagenomic analyses.

papers.title: The Causal Role of Gut Microbiota in Pulmonary Embolism and the Mediating Effects of Circulating Metabolites: A Mendelian Randomization Study.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota has been implicated in pulmonary vascular diseases, yet a direct causal link to pulmonary embolism (PE) remains unestablished. This study aimed to investigate the causal effects of gut microbiota on PE and to explore the mediating role of circulating metabolites in this relationship. We performed a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis using summary statistics from large-scale genome-wide association studies. The gut microbiota data were sourced from the MiBioGen consortium, PE data from the FinnGen consortium (R10), and metabolite data from a meta-analysis of 136
papers.summary: This study used Mendelian randomization to investigate whether gut microbiota composition causally influences pulmonary embolism (PE) risk, and whether circulating metabolites mediate this effect. The findings suggest specific microbial taxa may affect PE risk, with certain metabolites acting as mediators, providing new insights into the gut-lung axis in vascular disease.

papers.title: Natural transformation drives large-scale genome mosaicism in human gut bifidobacteria.
papers.abstract: Although horizontal gene transfer drives bacterial diversification, its contribution to chromosome-scale variation in human gut commensals remains unclear. This study demonstrated that human-associated bifidobacteria undergo extensive chromosomal transfer through natural transformation. Comparative genomics of coexisting Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum isolates from a single individual revealed extensive recombination signatures between the lineages. We experimentally reproduced this recombination by co-culturing strains, resulting in the transfer of multiple chromosomal regions and generati
papers.summary: This study reveals that natural transformation drives large-scale genome mosaicism in human gut bifidobacteria, as demonstrated by extensive chromosomal recombination between coexisting Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum isolates. The authors experimentally reproduced this recombination in co-cultures, showing that multiple chromosomal regions can be transferred, highlighting a key mechanism for bacterial diversification in the human gut.

papers.title: A three-metabolite microbiota-associated signature for early risk stratification of gestational diabetes mellitus.
papers.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and long-term metabolic and cardiovascular risk. However, oral glucose tolerance testing at 24-28 gestational weeks limits early risk stratification. Gut microbiota-associated metabolites may reflect early metabolic abnormalities, including those relevant to cardiometabolic health, but robust early-pregnancy biomarkers remain limited.
papers.summary: This study identifies a three-metabolite signature associated with gut microbiota that can stratify the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) early in pregnancy, potentially enabling earlier intervention than standard glucose tolerance testing. The findings highlight the role of microbial metabolites in early metabolic dysfunction and offer a promising non-invasive biomarker approach.

papers.title: The gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumors: Causal roles of microbiota and inflammatory proteins unveiled by Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: There is a growing number of research suggesting that there is an association between gut microbiota and central nervous system (CNS) tumor. However, the causal relationships and the mediation effects of inflammatory proteins in the associations are unclear. We extracted genetic variants associated with gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 4 subtypes of CNS tumors from published genome-wide association studies and performed a Mendelian randomization analysis to identify potential causal effects. The inverse variance weighted method was used as the main method. Mediation analysis and sing
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics to investigate causal links between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and CNS tumors. It identifies specific microbial taxa and inflammatory mediators that may influence tumor risk, suggesting a gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumor development.

papers.title: Causal associations between gut microbiota and five common oral lesions: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have investigated the relationship between gut microbiota (GM) and oral lesions, but the reported associations across microbial taxa and oral conditions have been inconsistent. This 2-sample Mendelian randomization study using summary-level GWAS data aimed to clarify the causal links between GM and 5 oral conditions: loose teeth, toothache, bleeding gums, painful gums, and mouth ulcers. GM data were obtained from the MiBioGen consortium, while outcome data were derived from the Neale Lab and MRC-IEU consortium. We applied inverse variance weighted (IVW) and complementary MR me
papers.summary: This Mendelian randomization study used genetic data to assess whether gut microbiota composition causally influences five common oral conditions (loose teeth, toothache, bleeding gums, painful gums, and mouth ulcers). The findings suggest potential causal links between specific microbial taxa and these oral lesions, though the effects were modest and require further validation.

papers.title: Zoo gut plastispheres enable pathogen escape and adaptation.
papers.abstract: In zoos, intensive human contact and artificial feeding may create pathways for microplastic (MP) ingestion and gut colonization. We hypothesized that ingested MPs form intestinal plastispheres with elevated pathogenic potential and enhanced environmental persistence. To test this, we surveyed feces from 15 zoo-dwelling species and coupled particle characterization, feces-derived intestinal simulations, metagenomic sequencing, and a subsequent water-exposure experiment. Zoo feces contained more abundant MPs than reported for wild counterparts, with fragments predominating and polyethylene tere
papers.summary: This study investigates microplastic (MP) particles in the feces of zoo animals, finding higher MP abundance than in wild counterparts and showing that these ingested MPs form 'plastispheres'—microbial communities with elevated pathogenic potential and environmental persistence. Using metagenomics and simulations, the authors demonstrate that zoo gut plastispheres can enable pathogen escape and adaptation, highlighting a potential health risk in human-animal interfaces.

papers.title: Human wastewater contamination drives the emergence of multidrug-resistant bacteria in the Galápagos marine ecosystem.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance poses a global threat to public health. Mobile microbiological laboratories can enable environmental monitoring of antimicrobial resistance, particularly in geographically remote and resource-limited locations, such as the Galápagos archipelago. Here, we report the development of a mobile laboratory for antimicrobial resistance surveillance of marine sites surrounding San Cristóbal, the archipelago's second most populated island, which has experienced rapid urbanization and intense international tourism pressure. On-site metagenomic sequencing of wastewater-contaminate
papers.summary: This study used a mobile laboratory to perform on-site metagenomic sequencing of marine samples around San Cristóbal Island in the Galápagos, revealing that human wastewater contamination is driving the emergence of multidrug-resistant bacteria in the marine ecosystem. The findings highlight the utility of portable lab setups for antimicrobial resistance surveillance in remote, resource-limited regions and underscore the environmental impact of urbanization and tourism.

papers.title: Biological contributions to manganese oxides in rock varnish at Murujuga (Western Australia).
papers.abstract: Rock varnish is a ubiquitous Mn-rich coating on exposed rock surfaces in arid environments, yet the mechanisms underlying its formation remain debated. Here, we investigate rock varnish from Murujuga, Western Australia, to assess the role of microbial processes in manganese (Mn) accumulation. Bulk compositional and mineralogical analyses confirm high concentrations of Mn, Fe, Al, and Si; however, the Mn matrix is predominantly composed of amorphous to poorly crystalline phases that fall below the indexing or detection thresholds of X-ray diffraction (XRD) and electron backscatter diffraction (
papers.summary: This study investigates the formation of manganese-rich rock varnish in arid Western Australia, finding that the Mn matrix is largely amorphous and poorly crystalline, with evidence suggesting microbial processes contribute to Mn accumulation. The findings challenge purely abiotic mechanisms and highlight the biological role in varnish formation.

papers.title: Establishment of an in vitro aerobic bacterial community as a model of the human lung microbiome.
papers.abstract: The human lung microbiome is increasingly recognized as a key player in drug metabolism, yet it remains largely understudied. To replicate this complex physiological environment in a controlled setting, we developed a simplified artificial lung microbiome model composed of four representative bacterial species: Pseudomonas koreensis, Rothia aeria, Neisseria cinerea, and Streptococcus downei. We successfully established a stable 10-day co-culture at 34°C using brain heart infusion medium, as validated by quantitative PCR, viability PCR, and conventional microbiological methodologies. Integrated
papers.summary: The authors developed a simplified in vitro model of the human lung microbiome using four representative bacterial species, which remained stable over 10 days in co-culture. This model provides a controlled system to study lung microbiome functions, such as drug metabolism, in a laboratory setting.

papers.title: Microbiota-Neuroinflammation Crosstalk in Primary Brain Tumors: Focus on Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults and remains difficult to treat because of diffuse invasion, immunosuppression, metabolic adaptability, and therapy resistance. This review evaluates how gut microbiota and microbiota-associated neuroinflammatory signaling may contribute to GBM biology and therapeutic response.
papers.summary: This review explores the emerging link between gut microbiota and neuroinflammation in glioblastoma (GBM), the most aggressive adult brain tumor. It discusses how microbiota-associated signaling may influence GBM progression, immunosuppression, and therapy resistance, suggesting a potential avenue for microbiome-based therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies microbial dysbiosis and functional metabolic reprogramming in acute kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening syndrome with high morbidity and mortality, yet its early diagnosis and underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. Emerging evidence implicates gut dysbiosis and microbial metabolic dysfunction in AKI pathogenesis via the gut-kidney axis, yet a comprehensive, multi-omics characterization of microbial functional alterations in general AKI populations remains lacking.
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative multi-omics approach to characterize gut microbial dysbiosis and functional metabolic reprogramming in patients with acute kidney injury (AKI), revealing specific microbial and metabolic alterations linked to the gut-kidney axis. The findings provide a comprehensive resource that may aid in early diagnosis and understanding of AKI pathogenesis.

papers.title: Fish gut-water interface as a hotspot for the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes across natural and aquaculture systems.
papers.abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are important reservoirs and transmission pathways for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet host-mediated microbial selection and anthropogenic pressure on fish gut resistome remain poorly characterised, especially in major South Asian river systems. We performed shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved binning from 194 fish representing four species, along with host-associated water samples, collected from six geographically distinct sites spanning two major river systems (the Yamuna and the Indus) and two aquaculture farms. The fish gut nurtures distinct microbial co
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved binning on 194 fish and associated water samples from South Asian rivers and aquaculture farms to show that the fish gut-water interface is a hotspot for antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) dissemination. The fish gut harbors distinct microbial communities that facilitate ARG exchange with the surrounding water, with anthropogenic pressure from aquaculture amplifying this spread.

papers.title: Functional genetic signatures of the gut microbiome in cardiometabolic diseases: mechanisms and translational opportunities.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome plays a very important role in the regulation of host metabolism and overall physiological homeostasis. Disruptions in microbial community function have been increasingly implicated in cardiometabolic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease. Advances in metagenomic sequencing have identified functional genetic signatures within the gut microbiome for short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis, bile acid metabolism, lipopolysaccharide (LPS) production, amino acid metabolism, trimethylamine N-oxide
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on how functional genetic signatures of the gut microbiome—such as those involved in short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis, bile acid metabolism, and LPS production—contribute to cardiometabolic diseases. It highlights mechanistic insights and discusses translational opportunities for microbiome-based diagnostics and therapeutics.

papers.title: Rhizosphere microbiomes in drought-tolerant and drought-sensitive bermudagrass genotypes: root exudate association.
papers.abstract: Plant-microbiome interactions in the rhizosphere are critical for plant adaptation to environmental stress; however, the coordinated roles of root exudates and microbiome dynamics remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study compares the rhizosphere microbiomes of drought-tolerant and drought-sensitive bermudagrass genotypes, revealing that drought-tolerant plants recruit distinct microbial communities associated with their root exudate profiles. The findings suggest that specific exudates shape the microbiome to enhance drought adaptation, providing insights into plant-microbiome interactions under stress.

papers.title: Omics data in relative values are almost subcompositionally coherent.
papers.abstract: Omics data are compositional and often expressed as relative abundances after total sum scaling normalization. An important statistical issue with compositional data is the lack of subcompositional coherence, meaning that relative abundances change when data are re-normalized after removing or adding features. While this problem is well documented for small compositions, it has not been investigated in large Omics datasets, which typically contain hundreds or thousands of features and where subcompositions are ubiquitous. Subcompositions arise, for example, when using different reference datas
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether the lack of subcompositional coherence—a known issue in compositional data analysis—is practically relevant for large omics datasets with hundreds or thousands of features. The authors show that relative abundances are almost subcompositionally coherent in such large datasets, meaning that re-normalization after adding or removing features has minimal impact, thus mitigating a common statistical concern.

papers.title: Calibrating tetranucleotide-frequency distances for metagenomic binning with right-skewed distribution models.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic binning is a pivotal step in reconstructing metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from complex microbial communities, and it critically depends on reliable measures of similarity between contigs. In many workflows, tetranucleotide-frequency (TNF) distances are translated into probabilistic evidence of a shared genome of origin. Despite their central role, these distances are often modeled with convenient but poorly matched assumptions, even though they are intrinsically non-negative and frequently exhibit pronounced right-skewness-features that can distort tail behavior and weaken do
papers.summary: This paper addresses a key limitation in metagenomic binning by showing that tetranucleotide-frequency (TNF) distances are often modeled with inappropriate distributional assumptions, despite being non-negative and right-skewed. The authors propose calibrating TNF distances using right-skewed distribution models, which improves the accuracy of probabilistic evidence for contig clustering and genome reconstruction.

papers.title: Effects of diarrhea and antibiotic-induced microbial elimination on dynamic changes in fecal microbial communities and antibiotic resistance of Hu sheep lambs (Ovis aries).
papers.abstract: As a highly reproductive meat sheep breed in China, Hu sheep is an important economic group in ruminant animal breeding. However, research on its intestinal microbiomes under the background of diarrhea and antibiotic treatment remains relatively limited.
papers.summary: This study examines how diarrhea and antibiotic treatment alter the fecal microbial communities and antibiotic resistance profiles of Hu sheep lambs, a key meat sheep breed in China. The findings reveal dynamic changes in microbial composition and resistance genes, providing insights into the impact of antibiotic use on gut health in this economically important livestock.

papers.title: The composition alteration of gut microbiota in lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The association between the gut microbiota and lung cancer remains understudied. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis to quantitatively synthesize evidence from multiple cohorts to identify robust and consistent alterations in gut microbial diversity and taxonomy associated with lung cancer.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes evidence from multiple cohorts to identify consistent alterations in gut microbial diversity and taxonomy associated with lung cancer. The findings provide a robust overview of gut microbiota changes in lung cancer patients, highlighting potential microbial markers and avenues for future research.

papers.title: Metagenomic and metabolomic profiling in primary aldosteronism with coexisting obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.abstract: Primary aldosteronism (PA) frequently coexists with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), and this comorbidity is associated with increased cardiometabolic risk. Although both PA and OSA have been individually linked to gut microbiome alterations, it remains unclear which layer of gut microbiome-associated variation best reflects clinical heterogeneity in PA with coexisting OSA.
papers.summary: This study profiles the gut microbiome and metabolome in patients with primary aldosteronism (PA) who also have obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), aiming to identify which microbial or metabolic features best reflect clinical heterogeneity in this comorbidity. The findings reveal distinct metagenomic and metabolomic signatures associated with the coexistence of PA and OSA, potentially offering biomarkers for risk stratification.

papers.title: Characterizing the parvovirome of Swazi bats: novel species, highly divergent lineages, endogenous viral elements, and taxonomic challenges.
papers.abstract: Parvoviridae (small, nonenveloped ssDNA viruses) currently includes 281 species in two vertebrate- and four invertebrate-infecting subfamilies. While parvovirus-derived sequences are frequently identified in viromes, their taxonomy and host affiliation can be challenging due to high host and genetic diversity. We investigated the faecal parvovirome of 46 bats (7 insectivorous and 1 frugivorous species) from Eswatini and identified 28 novel viral species in 29 individuals (63.0%). The majority of these (22/28, 78.6%) belonged to nine genera (including two that are previously undescribed) within
papers.summary: This study characterizes the parvovirus diversity in fecal samples from bats in Eswatini, identifying 28 novel viral species, including two previously undescribed genera, and highlighting the challenges in taxonomy and host assignment due to high genetic diversity and the presence of endogenous viral elements. The findings expand the known parvovirome and underscore the need for refined classification approaches in highly diverse viral families.

papers.title: Dynamics of archaeal diversity and functionality in the piglet gut microbiome under common antimicrobial treatments.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota comprises a diverse and dynamic community of microorganisms that collectively enhance host metabolism, physiology, and overall functionality. In this context, the swine archaeome remains largely underexplored despite growing evidence that archaea may greatly influence host health. Advances in high-throughput approaches provide new opportunities to reveal the dynamics and composition of archaea. Herein, we uncover the taxonomic and functional landscape of the piglet archaeome during the weaning transition under multiple experimental conditions, integrating shotgun metagenomic
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study characterizes the archaeal community (archaeome) in the piglet gut microbiome during weaning, revealing its taxonomic and functional dynamics under different antimicrobial treatments. Using shotgun metagenomics, the authors uncover how common antimicrobials shape archaeal diversity and functional potential, providing new insights into an understudied component of the gut microbiota.

papers.title: Long-reads metagenomics reveals the effects of dulse supplementation on the poultry caecal bacteriome and its associated genetic repertoire.
papers.abstract: Dulse (Palmaria palmata) is a macroalgal feed ingredient rich in polysaccharides and bioactive compounds that offers a sustainable strategy to enhance animal health and productivity through modulation of gut microbiota. However, the impact of dulse supplementation on the taxonomic composition and genetic repertoire of the broiler chicken caecal microbiota remains poorly characterised.
papers.summary: This study uses long-read metagenomics to investigate how supplementing broiler chicken feed with dulse (a red macroalga) affects the caecal microbiome and its genetic potential. The findings reveal changes in the bacteriome composition and associated functional genes, providing insights into the prebiotic potential of dulse as a sustainable feed additive.

papers.title: Shotgun metagenomic analysis reveals taxonomic and functional alterations in the gut microbiome across prodromal and symptomatic Lewy body disease.
papers.abstract: Lewy body disease (LBD) is a progressive neurodegenerative a-synucleinopathy, whereas isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) is recognized as a prodromal stage of LBD. Although growing evidence implicates the gut-brain axis in neurodegeneration, the taxonomic and functional roles of the gut microbiome across the prodromal-to-symptomatic LBD continuum remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomics to compare the gut microbiome across the prodromal (iRBD) and symptomatic stages of Lewy body disease, revealing distinct taxonomic and functional alterations that may be linked to disease progression. The findings suggest that gut microbial changes occur early in the disease continuum and could serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: GUT MICROBIOTA ALTERATIONS IN RODENT MODELS OF CHOLESTASIS INDUCED BY BILE DUCT LIGATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW.
papers.abstract: Cholestatic liver diseases are a major public health issue, marked by impaired bile flow and significant disruptions in liver and systemic physiology. Growing evidence points to the gut microbiota as a key player in cholestasis pathogenesis through gut-liver axis interactions. This systematic review aimed to synthesize and evaluate current findings on intestinal microbiota changes in rodents (rats and mice) subjected to bile duct ligation (BDL)-induced cholestasis, focusing on microbial diversity, taxonomic shifts, and potential pathophysiological implications.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence from rodent models of bile duct ligation-induced cholestasis, revealing consistent gut microbiota alterations including reduced diversity and shifts in specific bacterial taxa. These changes are linked to gut-liver axis dysfunction, suggesting the microbiota may play a role in cholestasis pathogenesis.

papers.title: From diversity to function: microbiome-mediated plant growth promotion, secondary metabolism, and antimicrobial resistance in Rauwolfia serpentina.
papers.abstract: This study presents the first metagenomic analysis of the root and rhizosphere microbiomes of Rauvolfia serpentina, an endangered medicinal plant. Metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the diverse microbial communities and their functional attributes to assess the ecological and biotechnological potential of this plant-associated microbiome.
papers.summary: This study provides the first metagenomic analysis of the root and rhizosphere microbiomes of the endangered medicinal plant Rauwolfia serpentina, revealing diverse microbial communities and their functional potential. The findings highlight microbiome-mediated plant growth promotion, secondary metabolism, and antimicrobial resistance, offering insights into the ecological and biotechnological significance of this plant-associated microbiome.

papers.title: Cigarette Butts as an Emerging Urban Habitat Driving Microbial Niche Differentiation.
papers.abstract: Cigarette butts are common yet overlooked pollutants in urban environments. How this anthropogenic niche shapes microbial life-history strategies and evolutionary mechanisms remains poorly understood, limiting assessments of microbial adaption and urban ecosystem health. However, systematic and multiscale evidence on the ecological effects of cigarette butts on microbial communities remains scarce. Here, we collected cigarette butts, litter, and soil samples from urban parks in 35 Chinese cities and integrated third-generation 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing, metagenomics, and transcriptomics to
papers.summary: This study investigates cigarette butts as a novel anthropogenic habitat in urban environments, using multi-omics approaches (16S rRNA sequencing, metagenomics, transcriptomics) on samples from 35 Chinese cities. The findings reveal that cigarette butts drive microbial niche differentiation, shaping distinct microbial life-history strategies and evolutionary mechanisms compared to surrounding litter and soil.

papers.title: Euonymus alatus in diabetes: a review of phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics, and anti-diabetic mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Euonymus alatus: (EA), a traditional Chinese botanical drug documented in the Shennong Ben Cao Jing, has been investigated for its potential anti-diabetic effects. This review systematically examines the phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics, and anti-diabetic mechanisms of this botanical drug. Over 230 metabolites, including flavonoids, triterpenoids, and lignans, have been identified from EA. Pharmacokinetic studies remain limited; computational predictions suggest that some metabolites may exhibit oral bioavailability, but classical pharmacokinetic parameters have not been experimentally determi
papers.summary: This review summarizes the phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics, and anti-diabetic mechanisms of the traditional Chinese herb Euonymus alatus, cataloging over 230 metabolites such as flavonoids, triterpenoids, and lignans. It highlights that while computational predictions suggest some metabolites may be orally bioavailable, experimental pharmacokinetic data are still lacking, underscoring the need for further research to validate its therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Effects of Urolithin A supplementation on muscle health outcomes in humans from randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: Urolithin A (UA), a gut microbiota-derived metabolite, has been proposed to improve skeletal muscle function, but evidence from randomized controlled trials has not been systematically summarized. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of UA supplementation on muscle performance as well as biochemical and mitochondrial biomarkers in humans.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates randomized controlled trials on the effects of Urolithin A (UA) supplementation on muscle health in humans. The findings suggest that UA may improve muscle performance and mitochondrial biomarkers, though the evidence is limited and warrants further investigation.

papers.title: Bacteria-related signals in brain metastases: evidence boundaries, tumor-microenvironment remodeling, and translational prospects.
papers.abstract: Brain metastases (BrM) develop within a highly specialized central nervous system niche shaped by the blood-brain barrier/blood-tumor barrier, brain-resident stromal cells, myeloid populations, and distinct metabolic constraints. Emerging studies suggest that bacteria-related signals can be detected in primary and metastatic brain tumors; however, their biological meaning remains incompletely defined. In particular, low-biomass brain tissues are highly vulnerable to reagent contamination, environmental carry-over, batch effects, and bioinformatic misclassification, making it essential to disti
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This review examines the emerging but uncertain role of bacteria-related signals in brain metastases, emphasizing the technical challenges of studying low-biomass brain tissues where contamination and bioinformatic artifacts can easily confound results. It discusses how these signals might influence the tumor microenvironment and highlights the need for rigorous methods to distinguish true microbial contributions from noise, while exploring potential translational implications.

papers.title: Recombinant Bacillus subtilis spores expressing cholera toxin B and ovalbumin prevent ovalbumin-specific food allergy in mice by upregulating regulatory T cells and modulating gut microbiome flora.
papers.abstract: Although oral immunotherapy has shown clinical efficacy in treating food allergies, its broader implementation is constrained by the occurrence of adverse effects. Consequently, inducing allergen-specific immune tolerance during early life can be a preventive strategy to reduce the development of food allergy.
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that recombinant Bacillus subtilis spores expressing cholera toxin B and ovalbumin can prevent ovalbumin-specific food allergy in mice by upregulating regulatory T cells and modulating the gut microbiome. The findings suggest a potential preventive strategy for food allergy that avoids the adverse effects associated with oral immunotherapy.

papers.title: Dietary index for gut microbiota score is inversely associated with carotid calcified plaque score in ischemic stroke patients.
papers.abstract: Diet influences gut microbiota-derived metabolites, which may affect vascular inflammation and calcification. The Dietary Index for Gut Microbiota (DI-GM) captures dietary patterns hypothesized to support favorable microbial metabolite profiles. In this study, we examined whether higher DI-GM scores are associated with lower carotid calcification burden in ischemic stroke patients and whether trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) is statistically associated with this relationship, without implying causality.
papers.summary: This study found that a higher Dietary Index for Gut Microbiota (DI-GM) score, reflecting a diet that supports beneficial gut microbes, is associated with a lower burden of carotid artery calcification in ischemic stroke patients. The relationship may involve the gut-derived metabolite TMAO, though the study does not establish causality.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium- and Escherichia-dominant ecological guilds shape altered microbial metabolic capacity of the gut microbiome in tuberculosis patients.
papers.abstract: The gut microbial community plays a key role in maintaining the host immune homeostasis. However, current analytical approaches analyze individual taxa rather than gut communities, thereby missing community-level functions performed by units, such as ecological guilds. Delineating ecological units is a promising approach for summarizing the functional output of microbes and their impact on the host.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study identifies distinct ecological guilds dominated by Bifidobacterium and Escherichia in the gut microbiomes of tuberculosis patients, showing that these community-level units have altered metabolic capacities compared to healthy controls. The findings highlight the importance of analyzing microbial communities as functional guilds rather than individual taxa to understand host-microbe interactions in tuberculosis.

papers.title: Low energy availability, the gut microbiome, and bone health in athletes: a mechanistic narrative review based on athlete evidence and clinical analogues.
papers.abstract: Low energy availability (LEA) is a central aetiological factor in Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs) and is frequently associated with impaired skeletal health in athletic populations, although skeletal responses can be heterogeneous. However, athletes with apparently similar energetic and training exposures can differ in bone mineral density, bone turnover and bone stress injury risk, indicating that additional physiological mediators may modify the skeletal response to under-fuelling. The gut microbiome has emerged as a plausible candidate because microbial metabolites, intestinal ba
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes that the gut microbiome may mediate the heterogeneous skeletal responses to low energy availability (LEA) in athletes, potentially explaining why athletes with similar energetic exposures differ in bone health outcomes. The authors synthesize evidence from athlete studies and clinical analogues to support a mechanistic link between under-fuelling, microbial metabolites, and bone metabolism.

papers.title: Magnolia biondii-Derived Exosome-Like Nanoparticles Ameliorate Ulcerative Colitis by Suppressing Inflammation, Reducing Oxidative Stress, and Modulating Gut Microbiota.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory bowel disease with limited treatment options and suboptimal remission rates. Plant-derived exosome-like nanoparticles have emerged as promising therapeutic agents due to their natural origin, biocompatibility, and capacity to deliver bioactive cargo. This study aimed to isolate exosome-like nanoparticles from the decoction of Magnolia biondii flower buds (Xinyi) (MFELNs) and evaluate their therapeutic potential in a murine model of UC.
papers.summary: This study isolated exosome-like nanoparticles from Magnolia biondii flower buds and tested them in a mouse model of ulcerative colitis. The nanoparticles reduced inflammation and oxidative stress and modulated gut microbiota, suggesting a potential new therapeutic approach for UC.

papers.title: Enterococcus faecium pneumonia diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing in a patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
papers.abstract: Enterococcus faecium is a rare pathogen in community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), and its diagnosis is challenging, particularly when prior antibiotic therapy hampers isolation by conventional culture. We report a 72-year-old man with a 6-year history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who presented with fever, cough, and progressive dyspnea. Despite empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam followed by imipenem-cilastatin), his condition deteriorated into acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. All routine cultures of
papers.summary: This case report describes a 72-year-old COPD patient with severe community-acquired pneumonia caused by Enterococcus faecium, a rare pathogen, which was diagnosed using metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) after conventional cultures failed due to prior antibiotic treatment. The case highlights the utility of mNGS for identifying uncommon pathogens in complex respiratory infections, especially when standard diagnostic methods are inconclusive.

papers.title: Diversity and taxonomic differences in the oral microbiota of stroke patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: In recent years, a growing body of evidence suggests that stroke may be associated with an imbalance in the oral microbiome. To further elucidate this potential link, this study aims to systematically compare differences in the oral microbiome between stroke patients and healthy individuals.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis compares the oral microbiome of stroke patients with healthy controls, finding significant diversity and taxonomic differences. The results support a potential link between oral microbial imbalance and stroke, highlighting the need for further research into causal mechanisms and therapeutic implications.

papers.title: Global research landscape and trends of metabolomics in diabetic kidney disease: focus on immunometabolic interactions.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a devastating microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus, arises from intricate crosstalk between metabolic disorders and immune dysregulation. Metabolomics has emerged as a powerful tool to unravel the immunometabolic mechanisms underlying DKD, facilitating early disease diagnosis, mechanistic pathway interpretation, and therapeutic biomarker discovery. This study aimed to systematically delineate the global research landscape and evolutionary trends of DKD metabolomics, with a key emphasis on immunometabolic interactions.
papers.journal: Frontiers in clinical diabetes and healthcare
papers.summary: This paper provides a systematic review of the global research landscape and trends in metabolomics applied to diabetic kidney disease (DKD), with a specific focus on immunometabolic interactions. It highlights how metabolomics is being used to uncover the complex crosstalk between metabolic and immune dysregulation, aiding in early diagnosis and biomarker discovery.

papers.title: Optimized protocol for profiling mucosa-associated microbiota from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded gut tissues from treatment-naïve pediatric patients with Crohn's disease.
papers.abstract: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues are yet underutilized resources for microbiome studies. Data on the mucosa-associated microbiota (MAM) of patients with Crohn's disease (CD) are scarce, due to several methodological limitations. In this study, we aimed to develop and validate a new optimized amplicon-based workflow to profile MAM from FFPE gut biopsies of pediatric CD patients.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This paper presents a new optimized amplicon-based workflow for profiling mucosa-associated microbiota from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) gut biopsies, addressing a key methodological gap in microbiome research. The protocol was validated on treatment-naïve pediatric Crohn's disease patients, enabling the use of underutilized FFPE tissues for studying host-microbe interactions in inflammatory bowel disease.
